summary: Craig Mathieson's guide to December 2023 streaming notes that streamers are again licensing content non-exclusively, as with Yellowjackets moving from Paramount+ to Netflix. He picks a top show for each service, including Maestro on Netflix, Strife on Binge, Bump on Stan, Reacher on Amazon Prime and The Snoopy Show on Apple TV+. He adds secondary picks and November highlights for each platform.
one_line: Craig Mathieson recommends the best December 2023 streaming shows across Netflix, Binge, Stan, Amazon Prime and Apple TV+, with a top pick per service.
key_facts: Mathieson says streaming's walls are crumbling, as streamers again sell non-exclusive rights to chase income.
Yellowjackets, a Paramount+ original with a third season commissioned, arrives on Netflix on December 15.
Netflix's top pick is Maestro (December 20), in which Bradley Cooper co-writes, directs and stars as conductor-composer Leonard Bernstein, with Carey Mulligan as Felicia Montealegre.
Zack Snyder's Rebel Moon: Part One – A Child of Fire arrives on Netflix on December 22; the sequel is scheduled for next April.
Binge's top pick is Strife (December 6), based on Mia Freedman's 2017 memoir Work Strife Balance, with Asher Keddie as Evelyn Jones and created by Sarah Scheller.
Vigil's second season arrives on Binge on December 11, with Suranne Jones and Rose Leslie investigating a failed attack drone demonstration at a British army base.
Stan's top pick is Bump (December 26), the fourth season of the Kelsey Munro and Claudia Karvan comic-drama, released every Boxing Day.
Revealed: Ben Roberts-Smith Truth on Trial (December 10, Stan) is a feature-length documentary directed by Dora Weekley about the investigation by Nick McKenzie and Chris Masters.
Dr Death returns to Stan on December 22 as an anthology, with Edgar Ramirez as surgeon Paolo Macchiarini and Mandy Moore as journalist Benita Alexander.
Amazon Prime's top pick is Reacher (December 15), with Alan Ritchson adding more muscle for the new season.
Prisoner's Daughter (December 5, Amazon Prime) stars Brian Cox and Kate Beckinsale and is directed by Catherine Hardwicke.
Apple TV+'s top pick is The Snoopy Show: Happiness is Holiday Traditions (December 1), a special closing the third season, in which no adults are seen or heard.
Family Plan (December 15, Apple TV+) stars Mark Wahlberg as former master assassin Dan Morgan, with Michelle Monaghan and Ciaran Hinds.
